0.title: The Secret of Peace in Every Circumstance
0.overview:
Anxiety is one of the defining struggles of our age. Many people live with a constant low hum of worry about money, health, children, work, the future or the state of the world. Others face crippling anxiety that affects their sleep, bodies and relationships. At the same time, our culture constantly feeds discontent. Advertising, social media and comparison tell us that we need more, that others have it better and that we will be happy when our circumstances change.

Anxiety and discontent are closely related. Both come from looking at our circumstances and concluding that we cannot be at peace until something changes. Scripture offers a different path. Paul, writing from prison, said, I have learned in whatever situation I am to be content (Phil 4:11). And he promised that the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus (Phil 4:7).

This study does not offer quick fixes. Anxiety can have many causes, some physical, and those who struggle deeply need patient care, sometimes including medical help. But Scripture speaks with deep comfort to anxious and discontented hearts, pointing us to a Father who knows what we need and a peace that circumstances cannot take away.

Five units: (1) The Anxious Heart; (2) Casting Our Cares on God; (3) Learning Contentment; (4) The Enemies of Contentment; (5) Peace in the Storm. The Biblical Counseling study has a fuller unit on caring for those with anxiety.

1.title: The Anxious Heart
1.overview:
Jesus speaks to worriers. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said, Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on (Matt 6:25). He was speaking to ordinary people, many of them poor, for whom food and clothing were real concerns. He did not dismiss their needs. He pointed them to their Father.

Look at the birds and the lilies. Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? (Matt 6:26). God clothes the flowers of the field with more beauty than Solomon's robes. If he cares for birds and grass, he will care for his children. Anxiety often forgets who our Father is.

Worry cannot add a single hour. And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to his span of life? (Matt 6:27). Worry promises control but delivers none. It borrows tomorrow's trouble and spoils today. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble (Matt 6:34).

Not all concern is sin. Paul spoke of the daily pressure on me of my anxiety for all the churches (2 Cor 11:28). Caring deeply about people and responsibilities is not sinful. Jesus himself was greatly distressed and troubled in Gethsemane (Mark 14:33). Scripture distinguishes between responsible concern, which leads us to pray and act, and anxious worry, which assumes the worst and forgets God.

A mixture of causes. Anxiety is often a mixture of legitimate fear (we live in a dangerous world), distorted fear (threats magnified beyond their reality) and unbelief (trusting something other than God for our safety). It can also have physical contributors such as illness, exhaustion or hormonal changes. Wise care addresses all of these, with patience.

Honest lament. The psalmists were not afraid to admit their inner turmoil. Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God; for I shall again praise him (Ps 42:5). They spoke honestly to God, and then they spoke truth to their own souls.
1.theology:
Anxiety and the Father: Jesus' argument depends on the fatherhood of God. Your heavenly Father knows that you need them all (Matt 6:32). The cure for anxiety is not positive thinking but a deeper knowledge of the Father's care. Unbelievers seek after all these things; children of God can trust their Father.

Seek first the kingdom: Jesus' alternative to anxiety is not passivity but priority: But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you (Matt 6:33). Anxiety shrinks when our hearts are set on God's purposes rather than our own security.

Gentleness with the anxious: Christians struggling with anxiety should not be made to feel that they are simply faithless. Jesus spoke gently to his anxious disciples, calling them little flock (Luke 12:32). Rebuke without comfort only adds to the burden.
1.examples:
Then: Martha welcomed Jesus into her home and was distracted with much serving. She complained that her sister Mary was not helping. Jesus answered gently: Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is necessary (Luke 10:40-42). Mary had chosen to sit at his feet. Jesus did not condemn Martha's service, but he called her to what mattered most.

Now: A young mother lies awake at night worrying about her children's health, the family finances and her own inadequacy. She feels guilty for worrying, which makes her worry more. A friend sits with her, reads Matthew 6:25-34 and says, "Your Father knows. You don't have to carry this alone." They pray together. The worries do not vanish, but she sleeps better that night.

A simple test: What are you most anxious about right now? Have you told your Father about it?

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to his span of life? And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is alive and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith? Therefore do not be anxious, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?' For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. "Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus gives several reasons not to be anxious. Life is more than food. God feeds the birds and clothes the lilies. Worry cannot add an hour to life. Pagans worry about these things, but you have a heavenly Father who knows your needs. Seek his kingdom first, and take one day at a time. Every argument rests on who God is.

verseByVerse.quote: Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God; for I shall again praise him, my salvation and my God. My soul is cast down within me; therefore I remember you from the land of Jordan and of Hermon, from Mount Mizar. Deep calls to deep at the roar of your waterfalls; all your breakers and your waves have gone over me. By day the LORD commands his steadfast love, and at night his song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life. I say to God, my rock: "Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?" As with a deadly wound in my bones, my adversaries taunt me, while they say to me all the day long, "Where is your God?" Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God; for I shall again praise him, my salvation and my God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The psalmist is downcast and far from home. He feels forgotten by God and mocked by enemies. Yet he speaks to his own soul: why are you cast down? Hope in God. Twice he repeats this refrain (Ps 42:5, 11). Fighting anxiety often means talking back to our fears with the truth about God.

verseByVerse.quote: And he said to his disciples, "Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on. For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing. Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storehouse nor barn, and yet God feeds them. Of how much more value are you than the birds! And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to his span of life? If then you are not able to do as small a thing as that, why are you anxious about the rest? Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass, which is alive in the field today, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith! And do not seek what you are to eat and what you are to drink, nor be worried. For all the nations of the world seek after these things, and your Father knows that you need them. Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be added to you. "Fear not, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Luke's version of Jesus' teaching ends with a tender word: Fear not, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. God is not reluctant or stingy. He delights to give his children the greatest gift of all. If he has given us the kingdom, he will not withhold what we need.

verseByVerse.quote: Now as they went on their way, Jesus entered a village. And a woman named Martha welcomed him into her house. And she had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet and listened to his teaching. But Martha was distracted with much serving. And she went up to him and said, "Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her then to help me." But the Lord answered her, "Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Martha was busy with good things, but anxious and distracted. Mary sat at Jesus' feet and listened. Jesus said one thing is necessary, and Mary had chosen it. Anxiety often comes from busyness that crowds out time with Christ.

1.reflection:
What are the main sources of anxiety in your life right now?

Read Matthew 6:25-34. Which of Jesus' reasons not to worry speaks most to you?

What is the difference between responsible concern and anxious worry?

How can you talk back to your fears with the truth about God, as Psalm 42 does?

2.title: Casting Our Cares on God
2.overview:
Pray instead of worrying. Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God (Phil 4:6). Paul does not simply say "stop worrying." He gives an alternative: turn every worry into a prayer. Not some things, but everything. Anything big enough to worry about is big enough to pray about.

With thanksgiving. Paul adds thanksgiving to prayer. Gratitude shifts our focus from what we lack to what God has given. Thanking God for past faithfulness strengthens trust for present needs.

The promise of peace. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus (Phil 4:7). Paul does not promise that God will give us everything we ask for. He promises peace, a peace that does not depend on circumstances and that makes no sense to the world. And this peace guards our hearts like a soldier guarding a city.

Cast your anxieties on him. Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God so that at the proper time he may exalt you, casting all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you (1 Pet 5:6-7). Casting is a deliberate act, like throwing a heavy load onto someone stronger. And the reason is simple: he cares for you.

Trust in the face of fear. When I am afraid, I put my trust in you (Ps 56:3). David does not say he is never afraid. He says that when fear comes, he turns to God. Faith is not the absence of fear but the decision to trust God in the middle of it.

Burden-bearing God. Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you (Ps 55:22). God may not remove the burden immediately, but he promises to sustain us under it.
2.theology:
Prayer and God's sovereignty: We pray because God is sovereign. If he were not in control, prayer would be pointless. Because he rules all things and cares for us, prayer is the most reasonable response to anxiety.

The Lord is at hand: Just before Philippians 4:6, Paul writes, The Lord is at hand (Phil 4:5). This may mean the Lord is near in presence, or that his return is near. Either way, it is a reason not to be anxious.

Repeated casting: For many people, casting anxieties on God is not a single act but a daily or hourly practice. Each time the worry returns, we cast it again. This is not failure; it is faith exercised.
2.examples:
Then: When King Hezekiah received a threatening letter from the king of Assyria, he went up to the temple and spread it before the LORD (2 Kgs 19:14). Then he prayed. God answered and delivered Jerusalem. Hezekiah literally laid his anxiety before God.

Now: A man facing redundancy at work begins writing his worries in a notebook each morning, then turning each one into a prayer, and adding one thing he is thankful for. He still loses his job. But he finds himself surprisingly at peace, and three months later he finds new work. He keeps the notebook as a record of God's faithfulness.

A simple test: Take your biggest worry right now and turn it into a specific prayer, with thanksgiving.

verseByVerse.quote: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice. Let your reasonableness be known to everyone. The Lord is at hand; do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul writes from prison, facing possible execution. Yet he commands joy, gentleness and prayer instead of anxiety. The promise is the peace of God, guarding hearts and minds. This is not denial of trouble but trust in the God who is near.

verseByVerse.quote: Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God so that at the proper time he may exalt you, casting all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you. Be sober-minded; be watchful. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, firm in your faith, knowing that the same kinds of suffering are being experienced by your brotherhood throughout the world. And after you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will himself restore, confirm, strengthen, and establish you. To him be the dominion forever and ever. Amen. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter connects humility, casting our cares on God, watchfulness against the devil and endurance in suffering. The God of all grace will restore, confirm, strengthen and establish his people after they have suffered a little while. Anxiety is met by God's care and by the hope of his final restoration.

verseByVerse.quote: But I call to God, and the LORD will save me. Evening and morning and at noon I utter my complaint and moan, and he hears my voice. He redeems my soul in safety from the battle that I wage, for many are arrayed against me. God will give ear and humble them, he who is enthroned from of old, Selah because they do not change and do not fear God. My companion stretched out his hand against his friends; he violated his covenant. His speech was smooth as butter, yet war was in his heart; his words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords. Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David is betrayed by a close friend and overwhelmed. He calls to God evening, morning and noon. Then he urges others: cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved. The one who prayed in distress now encourages others to do the same.

verseByVerse.quote: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you. In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I shall not be afraid. What can flesh do to me? (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David wrote this psalm when the Philistines seized him in Gath. He admits his fear, but he chooses trust. In God, whose word he praises, he trusts and will not be afraid. What can flesh do to him? Trust in God puts human threats in perspective.

2.reflection:
Why does Paul tell us to pray "with thanksgiving"?

What does it mean that God's peace "guards" our hearts and minds?

Read 1 Peter 5:7. What anxiety do you need to cast on God today?

How can you make casting your cares on God a daily habit?

3.title: Learning Contentment
3.overview:
The secret Paul learned. Not that I am speaking of being in need, for I have learned in whatever situation I am to be content. I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound. In any and every circumstance, I have learned the secret of facing plenty and hunger, abundance and need. I can do all things through him who strengthens me (Phil 4:11-13). Contentment is not natural. Paul had to learn it. And it was not dependent on circumstances; he was content in both plenty and poverty.

Christ is enough. The secret of contentment is Christ himself. The famous verse I can do all things through him who strengthens me is not about achieving our dreams, but about being content in any circumstance through Christ's strength. When Christ is our treasure, we can be at peace with or without other things.

Godliness with contentment. But godliness with contentment is great gain, for we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out of the world. But if we have food and clothing, with these we will be content (1 Tim 6:6-8). Life is short, and we leave it with nothing. Contentment sees possessions in that light.

God's presence. Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, "I will never leave you nor forsake you." (Heb 13:5). The reason for contentment is not what we have but who we have. If God is with us, we have everything we need.

A good inheritance. David sang, The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot. The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, I have a beautiful inheritance (Ps 16:5-6). God himself is the portion of his people.

Contentment is not complacency. Contentment does not mean we never seek to improve our circumstances, pursue goals or work for change. It means our peace does not depend on those things. A content person can still pray for a spouse, look for a better job or seek healing, without being consumed by the longing.
3.theology:
Contentment and providence: Contentment rests on the belief that God governs our circumstances wisely and lovingly. What he has given is not an accident. What he has withheld, he has withheld for good reasons, even when we cannot see them. The Providence of God study explores this further.

Contentment and the future: Believers can be content now partly because they know what is coming. Present lack is temporary; future inheritance is eternal (1 Pet 1:4).

The danger of riches: Paul warns that those who desire to be rich fall into temptation, and that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils (1 Tim 6:9-10). Discontent with what we have can lead to debt, dishonesty and destruction.
3.examples:
Then: Paul and Silas, beaten and in stocks in a Philippian prison, were praying and singing hymns at midnight (Acts 16:25). Their circumstances could hardly have been worse. Yet they were content enough to sing. Paul later wrote to that same Philippian church about learning contentment.

Now: A couple in their thirties feel behind their friends: smaller house, older car, fewer holidays. They start a habit of naming three things they are grateful for at dinner each night. Over a year, they notice that they compare less and enjoy more. Their circumstances have not changed. Their hearts have.

A simple test: Finish the sentence: "I would be content if only..." What does your answer reveal?

verseByVerse.quote: I rejoiced in the Lord greatly that now at length you have revived your concern for me. You were indeed concerned for me, but you had no opportunity. Not that I am speaking of being in need, for I have learned, in whatever situation I am, to be content. I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound. In any and every circumstance, I have learned the secret of facing plenty and hunger, abundance and need. I can do all things through him who strengthens me. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul thanks the Philippians for their gift, but he makes clear that his contentment did not depend on it. He had learned to be content in hunger and plenty. The secret is Christ's strength. This verse is about contentment in every circumstance, not about achieving anything we set our minds to.

verseByVerse.quote: But godliness with contentment is great gain, for we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out of the world. But if we have food and clothing, with these we will be content. But those who desire to be rich fall into temptation, into a snare, into many senseless and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils. It is through this craving that some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many pangs. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Some people treated godliness as a way to get rich. Paul says godliness with contentment is the real gain. We came with nothing and will leave with nothing. Those who desire riches fall into traps, and the love of money has led some away from the faith. Contentment protects the soul.

verseByVerse.quote: Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, "I will never leave you nor forsake you." So we can confidently say, "The Lord is my helper; I will not fear; what can man do to me?" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The writer links contentment to God's presence. Be free from the love of money, because God has promised never to leave us. So we can say with confidence, The Lord is my helper; I will not fear. Contentment rests on a person, not on possessions.

verseByVerse.quote: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot. The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, I have a beautiful inheritance. I bless the LORD who gives me counsel; in the night also my heart instructs me. I have set the LORD always before me; because he is at my right hand, I shall not be shaken. Therefore my heart is glad, and my whole being rejoices; my flesh also dwells secure. For you will not abandon my soul to Sheol, or let your holy one see corruption. You make known to me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy; at your right hand are pleasures forevermore. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David's portion is the LORD himself. His boundaries are pleasant; his inheritance is beautiful. Because God is at his right hand, he will not be shaken. His heart is glad and his body rests secure. In God's presence there is fullness of joy. This is the deepest root of contentment.

3.reflection:
Why do you think Paul had to "learn" contentment?

What does Philippians 4:13 really mean in its context?

How does God's promise "I will never leave you" make contentment possible?

What are you grateful for today? Name at least five things.

4.title: The Enemies of Contentment
4.overview:
Contentment has enemies. Recognising them helps us fight them.

Covetousness. The tenth commandment says, You shall not covet (Exod 20:17). Covetousness is wanting what belongs to someone else, or wanting more than God has given, so much that it rules the heart. Jesus warned, Take care, and be on your guard against all covetousness, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions (Luke 12:15). Paul calls covetousness idolatry (Col 3:5), because it treats things as if they could give what only God gives.

Comparison. Asaph confessed, For I was envious of the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked (Ps 73:3). Comparison breeds envy, and envy kills contentment. Social media has made comparison constant: we see the highlights of others' lives and measure our ordinary days against them.

Grumbling. In the wilderness, Israel complained about food, water and leadership, even after seeing God's miracles. They longed for Egypt: We remember the fish we ate in Egypt that cost nothing, the cucumbers, the melons (Num 11:5). They forgot the slavery and remembered only the food. Grumbling rewrites the past and blinds us to present grace.

Forgetting God. Moses warned Israel that when they were prosperous in the land, they might forget the LORD and say, My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth (Deut 8:17). Prosperity can be as dangerous as poverty.

The cure. Asaph's envy was cured when he went into God's sanctuary and saw the end of the wicked (Ps 73:17). Then he said, Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire besides you (Ps 73:25). Contentment returns when God becomes our treasure again.
4.theology:
Covetousness and the heart: The tenth commandment is unique in addressing desire rather than action. It shows that God cares about the heart, not only behaviour. Paul said this commandment convicted him of sin (Rom 7:7).

Gratitude as weapon: Thanksgiving is one of the strongest weapons against discontent. It is hard to covet and give thanks at the same time.

Eternal perspective: Comparing ourselves with others makes sense only if this life is all there is. In light of eternity, the differences that seem so large now will appear very small.
4.examples:
Then: King Ahab had a palace and a kingdom, but he sulked on his bed because Naboth would not sell him his vineyard (1 Kgs 21:4). His covetousness led to Naboth's murder. A king with everything was miserable over one small field.

Now: A woman realises that every time she scrolls through social media, she feels dissatisfied with her home, body and life. She decides to take a break from it for a month and to spend that time reading Psalms and writing thank-you notes. At the end of the month, she is surprised how much more content she feels.

A simple test: Whom do you most often compare yourself with? What does that comparison do to your heart?

verseByVerse.quote: Truly God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart. But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled, my steps had nearly slipped. For I was envious of the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Asaph begins with a confession of faith: God is good to Israel. But then he admits that his feet almost slipped because he envied the prosperity of the wicked. Even believers who know the truth can be shaken by comparison. Honesty about envy is the first step to overcoming it.

verseByVerse.quote: But when I thought how to understand this, it seemed to me a wearisome task, until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I discerned their end. Truly you set them in slippery places; you make them fall to ruin. How they are destroyed in a moment, swept away utterly by terrors! Like a dream when one awakes, O Lord, when you rouse yourself, you despise them as phantoms. When my soul was embittered, when I was pricked in heart, I was brutish and ignorant; I was like a beast toward you. Nevertheless, I am continually with you; you hold my right hand. You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you will receive me to glory. Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire besides you. My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Asaph's perspective changed in God's sanctuary. He saw the end of the wicked: they are on slippery ground. Then he saw his own foolishness and God's faithfulness. God holds his right hand, guides him and will receive him to glory. His flesh and heart may fail, but God is his portion forever. This is the cure for envy.

verseByVerse.quote: Someone in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me." But he said to him, "Man, who made me a judge or arbitrator over you?" And he said to them, "Take care, and be on your guard against all covetousness, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions." And he told them a parable, saying, "The land of a rich man produced plentifully, and he thought to himself, 'What shall I do, for I have nowhere to store my crops?' And he said, 'I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. And I will say to my soul, "Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry."' But God said to him, 'Fool! This night your soul is required of you, and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?' So is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: A man asked Jesus to settle an inheritance dispute. Jesus refused, then warned against covetousness. He told the parable of the rich fool, who planned for himself and forgot God. Life does not consist in possessions. What matters is being rich toward God.

verseByVerse.quote: Now the rabble that was among them had a strong craving. And the people of Israel also wept again and said, "Oh that we had meat to eat! We remember the fish we ate in Egypt that cost nothing, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic. But now our strength is dried up, and there is nothing at all but this manna to look at." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The rabble among Israel had a strong craving, and soon all the people were weeping for meat. They remembered Egypt's food as if it had been free, and despised God's daily manna. Discontent made them ungrateful for miraculous provision. It can do the same to us.

4.reflection:
Which enemy of contentment is strongest in your life: covetousness, comparison, grumbling or forgetting God?

Read Psalm 73. What turned Asaph's heart around?

How does social media affect your contentment? What boundaries might help?

Write a short prayer of thanks for what God has given you.

5.title: Peace in the Storm
5.overview:
Jesus in the storm. A great storm arose on the Sea of Galilee. The disciples, experienced fishermen, were terrified. Jesus was asleep in the stern. They woke him: Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? He rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm. Then he asked them, Why are you so afraid? Have you still no faith? (Mark 4:38-40). The storm was real, but so was the presence of Christ in the boat.

Perfect peace. You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts in you (Isa 26:3). Peace comes from where our minds rest. Fixing our thoughts on God, rather than endlessly rehearsing our fears, brings peace.

God our refuge. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear though the earth give way (Ps 46:1-2). Even if everything collapses, God remains. Be still, and know that I am God (Ps 46:10).

Body and soul. God made us as whole people, and anxiety often affects and is affected by the body. When Elijah was exhausted and wanted to die, God first gave him sleep and food, twice, before speaking to him (1 Kgs 19:4-8). Rest, exercise, healthy eating and time outdoors are not unspiritual. For some, anxiety has medical causes or is severe enough to need a doctor's care. Medication, where appropriate, is a legitimate help, not a sign of weak faith. Body and soul both need attention.

Help from others. No one should face severe anxiety alone. Pastors, wise friends and counsellors can help. Sharing burdens is part of Christian love (Gal 6:2).

The final peace. Jesus said, Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid (John 14:27). His peace is a gift now, and it will be complete when he returns and every cause of fear is removed.
5.theology:
Peace with God and the peace of God: Believers have peace with God through justification (Rom 5:1). This is permanent. The peace of God, a felt calm in the heart, may come and go. But the first is the foundation of the second. Even on anxious days, our peace with God is secure.

Faith and feelings: Anxious feelings do not necessarily mean weak faith. Faith often acts while feelings lag behind. Trusting God in the middle of anxiety is real faith.

God's sovereignty in storms: Christ does not always calm the storm immediately. Sometimes he calms us in the storm. Either way, he is Lord of the wind and the waves.
5.examples:
Then: On the night before Peter's planned execution, he was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains (Acts 12:6). James had already been killed. Yet Peter slept. An angel had to strike him to wake him. His peace came from trusting God with his life.

Now: A Christian man has struggled with panic attacks for years and has felt ashamed to admit it. He finally tells his pastor, who encourages him to see his doctor. With medical help, counselling and a small group who pray for him, his anxiety slowly becomes manageable. He still has hard days, but he knows he is not alone, and that Christ is in the boat.

A simple test: Is there someone you could talk to about your anxieties, rather than carrying them alone?

verseByVerse.quote: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, "Let us go across to the other side." And leaving the crowd, they took him with them in the boat, just as he was. And other boats were with him. And a great windstorm arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling. But he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. And they woke him and said to him, "Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?" And he awoke and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Peace! Be still!" And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. He said to them, "Why are you so afraid? Have you still no faith?" And they were filled with great fear and said to one another, "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The disciples assumed Jesus did not care because he was asleep. In fact, he was completely in control. He calmed the storm with a word, and the disciples were filled with a greater fear, the awe of seeing who he was. Knowing who is in the boat changes everything.

verseByVerse.quote: You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts in you. Trust in the LORD forever, for the LORD GOD is an everlasting rock. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Perfect peace belongs to the one whose mind is fixed on God. The reason is given: because he trusts in God. Then Isaiah urges, Trust in the LORD forever, for the LORD GOD is an everlasting rock. Our peace rests on God's unchanging strength.

verseByVerse.quote: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear though the earth give way, though the mountains be moved into the heart of the sea, though its waters roar and foam, though the mountains tremble at its swelling. Selah There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy habitation of the Most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved; God will help her when morning dawns. The nations rage, the kingdoms totter; he utters his voice, the earth melts. The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah Come, behold the works of the LORD, how he has brought desolations on the earth. He makes wars cease to the end of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear; he burns the chariots with fire. "Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth!" The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This psalm imagines the worst: earth giving way, mountains falling into the sea, nations raging. Yet God is a refuge and strength. There is a river that makes glad the city of God. He makes wars cease. And he says, Be still, and know that I am God. In the midst of chaos, God's people can be still.

verseByVerse.quote: Then he was afraid, and he arose and ran for his life and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there. But he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness and came and sat down under a broom tree. And he asked that he might die, saying, "It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life, for I am no better than my fathers." And he lay down and slept under a broom tree. And behold, an angel touched him and said to him, "Arise and eat." And he looked, and behold, there was at his head a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. And he ate and drank and lay down again. And the angel of the LORD came again a second time and touched him and said, "Arise and eat, for the journey is too great for you." And he arose and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mount of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: After his great victory on Mount Carmel, Elijah fled in fear and asked to die. God did not rebuke him. He let him sleep, gave him food and water, and let him sleep again. Then he gave him strength for the journey. God cares for his exhausted servants gently, body and soul.

5.reflection:
Read Mark 4:35-41. What does this teach you about Christ's presence in your storms?

What does it mean for your mind to be "stayed" on God (Isa 26:3)?

How does God's care for Elijah show that body and soul both matter?

Who could you share your anxieties with this week?
